description:
## Mandatory context and boundaries
Read the parent epic first. Applicable owners: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md; docs/services/channels.md (communication/Jido bridge and provider contracts); docs/services/engine.md (history, admission, finalization and delivery). Read docs/documentation.md before documentation/skill edits, docs/services/system-config.md before credential fixtures, and local module @moduledoc before extending a helper. Apply code-quality for code and skill-creator for the skill.
Only test/ additions or backward-compatible support changes, lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex, and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/** are authorized. Do not edit application modules, dependency source/pins, config, migrations, mix.exs, CI, or unrelated skills. Existing-test expectation changes require the testing handbook's explicit approval; this epic authorizes additive coverage, not changing expectations.
Use real bridges, NodeRouter, Engine admission/history/persistence and configured Agent execution. Only provider/LLM boundaries are faked. A production defect is a reported blocker with a reproducer; do not patch production, silently omit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or close the issue as complete.
Validation timing, failure handling and final gates are owned by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Record executed commands/results in this issue. No new browser E2E is needed: this work adds test/developer infrastructure without changing a deployed UI journey. No commit/push/merge authorization is implied.

Parent epic: zaq-o9d

## Functional specification and files
Own new test/support/channels/integration/{driver,session,registry,contract}.ex and framework/driver contract tests under test/zaq/channels/integration/. Use Zaq.TestSupport.Channels.Integration as the namespace. Implement the parent epic's six callback signatures and handle/session/delivery/script schemas exactly. connect/2 is the deliberate second startup phase; do not hide pairing in a function-valued field or make start/1 persist ZAQ records.
Define callback specs and @moduledoc describing allowed side effects. Contract helpers validate shapes and observable behaviour, not only @behaviour declarations. Invalid start/result/capability/script shapes produce descriptive ExUnit failures naming provider and operation.
Registry.all/0 returns sorted {provider, driver_module} pairs. Use one literal @drivers keyword list between exactly one BEGIN CHANNEL INTEGRATION DRIVERS / END CHANNEL INTEGRATION DRIVERS comment pair; no runtime eval. This is the generator's only registration mutation point. Registry validation must find duplicate provider/module entries, absent callbacks, driver source files lacking an entry, and invalid required capabilities.
During staged implementation the registry grows as concrete driver issues land; do not register nonexistent modules. Framework tests use scoped temporary fixture modules/files to exercise registry validation. The all-provider suite issue establishes the final required Mattermost/Telegram/WhatsApp baseline. Future generator-created skeletons are registered immediately and intentionally fail until implemented.
A coverage-report function compares a supplied production provider registry with test drivers and returns tested/missing providers without claiming missing providers are covered. Scope the input to communication adapters using JidoChatBridge; do not pull ingestion/email/widget into this suite.

## Tests to add before implementation
- Valid driver and session; missing callback; malformed results; required direct/shared capability absent; duplicate provider/module; unregistered driver file.
- Registry order is deterministic; discovery is scoped to drivers/*.ex and expected namespaces; duplicate or ambiguous generated markers are rejected by the later generator.
- Required scenarios cannot be disabled by false capabilities. Optional capabilities return explicit unsupported evidence.
- Property tests over safe provider identifiers and ordering/duplicate invariants, using existing StreamData/ExUnitProperties only.
- Contract checks prove script responses/recorded native requests, not private call order or implementation-mirroring assertions.

## Branches/paths validated
Success and callback failure shapes, missing/duplicate registrations, empty interim registry versus final suite baseline, optional/mandatory capability classification, and tested/missing provider reporting.

## Mocking plan
Only small test-owned fake providers/adapter-contract fixtures are needed to prove the harness's own behaviour. No NodeRouter/Agent/Engine stubs in real round-trip cases. No application configuration changes are needed for pure validation tests.

## Documentation
Put the callback ownership, exact message/script/delivery fields, two-phase startup and registration rules in module docs and the new test README (draft this section now). Link repository testing policy; do not restate it in docs/.

## Action reuse assessment
Decision: local-only test contract and registry. Existing Jido.Chat.Adapter and AdapterTestKit validate production adapter APIs/capabilities but do not manage ZAQ fixture sessions, native ingress or canonical transcripts. Reuse compatible adapter assertions; keep this driver contract separate and test-owned. Consumers are ExUnit and the later generator/skill; no Jido Action, agent-tool or workflow exposure. Errors are test failures and state is session-scoped.

## Done when
Framework contract tests pass; six callbacks and exact return shapes are documented; registry has one deterministic edit point and explicit coverage gaps; all changes are in test/. Record validation under the workflow owner.

comments.text: Implemented the six-callback Driver behaviour, Session ownership struct, executable Contract validators, deterministic Registry with marked scaffold edit point and missing-provider coverage report, a stateful contract fixture, README and framework tests. Existing production/application files and helper expectations were untouched. Validation: focused mix test test/zaq/channels/integration/framework_contract_test.exs passed (7 tests, 1 property, 0 failures); canonical MIX_ENV=dev mix q passed (hooks, formatting, Credo, docs and warnings-as-errors compile). The initial cold test build timed out while compiling dependencies; subsequent runs completed. MIX_ENV=test mix q could not find dev-only docs tooling; corrected by using canonical dev environment. Registry remains empty during the staged foundation; drivers are added in .3/.4/.5 and the full suite then requires all three. No commit/push performed.

title: [zaq-o9d.1] Define driver/session contracts and deterministic test-driver registry
